items.title: Hundreds of deaths each week associated with A&E overcrowding, new research suggests
items.summary: 25/09/2026 - New research is yet more evidence that A&E overcrowding kills, but governments remain too slow to act, says the Royal College of Emergency Medicine (RCEM).

items.title: The Ideas Changing Emergency Medicine: RCEM’s 2026 Top Poster Winners
items.summary: Discover the research, quality improvement projects, innovations and case reports recognised among the top submissions at RCEM Annual Conference 2026.

items.title: RCEM welcomes rollout of Martha’s Rule to all A&Es in England
items.summary: 23/09/2026 - Martha’s Rule is being expanded to all Emergency Departments in England.

items.title: Royal College of Emergency Medicine reaffirms support for Advanced Clinical Practice in Emergency Departments
items.summary: 22/09/2026 - The Royal College of Emergency Medicine (RCEM) has today reaffirmed its strong support for Advanced Clinical Practice in Emergency Departments (EDs).

items.title: Bipolar in Emergency Medicine – Share Your Story
items.summary: This article contains discussion of suicidal thoughts, self-harm and mental illness. If you are affected by any of the issues discussed, please seek support from appropriate healthcare or professional support services.

items.title: Recognising the patterns: Dr Ismat shares his story of learning how to spot emotions in ED through his daughter
items.summary: Dr Ismat Borhan shares his story with us for National Inclusion Week UK. He tells us the importance of listening to the patient and their family to build a more accurate diagnosis.
